about: SchwingNet's claims register: every claim the talk, the provisional's draft, the grant, the manuscripts and the operating-room study make or mean to make, as the textbook's chapters and the artifacts record them, each with the evidence it stands on and its grade, and every outstanding experiment or open question as an item that says which claims it bears on and what it costs. tools/claims_rank.py ranks the items and checks that the file holds together; chapter 33 (docs/textbook/33-what-to-run-next-by-the-weight-of-the-claims.md) explains it. Written 2026-10-24 for issue #216. Confidential with the rest of this repository: it names what the provisional's claims can and cannot rest on.
grade_rules: A claim's grade is the weakest grade among its evidence. Measured: a number read here from a result file or computed by tested code. Reported: stated by an artifact, a paper or the earlier programme's records without the file behind it read here. Inferred: a judgment or a design claim with no outcome measured. Unverified: no source, or contradicted by another record. A novelty claim cannot be Measured, since nothing measures an absence: it is Unverified while a named prior-art item is unread or contradicts it, Inferred once the search is recorded and finds nothing against it, and Reported once counsel's written read says so.

claims.statement: Naming each vertebral level from a single intraoperative C-arm exposure, with no registration to a preoperative scan and no other image of the patient, has not been published.

evidence.note: none of the seven Johns Hopkins items names levels; a search, not a proof
Huang 2022 (cadaver Long-Film) and Zeng 2024 (intraoperative AP G-arm) already name levels on real images with no CT, so the claim holds only as the whole of it
Li 2016, Li 2017 and ABLSpineLevelCheck 2024 are listed unread because the publisher's site was blocked; any could hold a C-arm naming result

claims.statement: The talk's first-time claim: a per-level naming rate on real C-arm frames at any angle, as a per-angle curve, by a model with its own detector and no CT, with its latency measured; no published method reports that whole.

evidence.note: section 2: no comparator row reports a per-angle curve or a latency with level naming
section 6: what the talk may claim once measured, and may not claim (first from renders, first on C-arm frames)
